nodes.title: Breakfast
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. “Okay. I’ll take you to the bathroom now.” You carry {{Carl}} to the bathroom and run his bath, then settle him in his wheelchair and push him out along the balcony. “Anything special on the agenda today?” “Yes, there’s the opening of your retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art. The gallery director left four messages asking to confirm your attendance.” “I haven’t decided yet. We’ll see about that later.” “Okay.” “What else?” “Just your usual fan mail. I’ve already answered.” “Any news from {{Leo}}?” “No, {{Carl}}. I can call him if you like?” “No. No, don’t bother.” You take him down in the wheelchair elevator to the living room. “I’m starving.” “Well, your breakfast is ready. Bacon and eggs, just the way you like them.” “Thank you, {{Markus}}.” “You’re welcome.” You bring the tray from the kitchen and serve him at the dining table. “Thank you, {{Markus}}. Television.” The TV comes on with the news. You pour his coffee. “Why don’t you find something to do while I finish my breakfast?” “Sure… Okay, {{Carl}}.”

nodes.title: The news at breakfast

media.title: the news on the living-room TV
facts: The TV news: tensions are rising in the Arctic since Russia unilaterally declared the region part of its national territory; Russian warships have taken position in the Barents Sea and a Russian flag flies over the ice field. The United States says it will not accept the annexation under any circumstances, and American destroyers are reported headed for the Barents Sea. The chairman of the UN says the world has never been so close to a Third World War and calls on both countries to renew talks before things get out of control.

media.title: Century: The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It
facts: Century (cover: “Frozen treasures”; also “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) reports that Russia’s interest in the North Pole has intensified since precious minerals used in synthesizing thirium were found trapped in the ice; surplus reserves would let either the US or Russia build more advanced androids and greatly boost its military and industrial output. NATO says “A conflict would benefit nobody”; President {{Warren}}: “It’s simple. Russia has no business in the Arctic. If the Kremlin doesn’t understand that, we will make them understand.”

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Life Found on Titan!
facts: {{Detroit}} Today (cover: “Life Found on Titan!”; also “NATO Security Council divided over Arctic dispute”) reports that a probe launched nineteen years ago has confirmed microorganisms living hundreds of kilometers below Titan’s surface, in a salt-water ocean under thick ice; after similar finds on Enceladus, life may be common in the universe. NASA calls its android expedition to Io one of many voyages seeking extraterrestrial life, and {{CyberLife}} says its space-faring androids are specially designed for long-range missions of this kind.

nodes.title: {{Leo}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. You open your eyes. {{Carl}} is staring at your canvas. “Oh my God…” A voice from the doorway: “Hey, Dad.” A young man has walked into the studio. “{{Leo}}… I didn’t hear you come in…” “Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I’d stop by… It’s been awhile, right?” “You all right? You don’t look so good.” “Oh, yeah, yeah, I’m fine… Hey listen, uh… I need some cash, Dad.” “Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?” “Uh well, it just goes, you know?” “Yeah… Yeah, you’re on it again, aren’t you?” “No, no, no, I swear it’s not that…” “Don’t lie to me, {{Leo}}.” “What difference does it make? Every chart node in the bracket is an option, after the report to {{Hank}} (offered only once the investigation is complete), in the order of the police markers, then the bathroom (whose statue is the tenth evidence item; story 1.9.2 moved it up from among the other looks), and then the rest: ANALYZE CARLOS’ BODY (the template’s Body clues), RECONSTRUCT CARLOS’ LAST MOMENTS (needs the body), ANALYZE KNIFE (2), ANALYZE RED ICE (3), the blood at marker 4 (PowerPyx; no chart node of its own), ANALYZE BLOOD ON WALLS (two options, markers 5 and 6, as PowerPyx counts them), EXAMINE CHAIR (7), ANALYZE MISSING KNIFE (8), ANALYZE BASEBALL BAT (9; the template’s Bat clue), RECONSTRUCT ASSAULT WITH BAT (needs the bat), EXAMINE EDEN CLUB FLYER, ANALYZE BACKYARD (the template’s Prints clue; the shoe print reads K52 as in the template), INVESTIGATE WRITING, SAMPLE BLOOD (the template’s Blood clue; in the game any blood can be tasted once), OPEN CLOSET, CHECK SHOWER (chart state CONNOR KNOWS ABOUT RA9), EXAMINE STATUE (needs the shower; chart state CONNOR HAVE SEEN THE STATUE), READ “ANDROID SEX” and READ “ANDROID SPY” (the two magazines are options here, not a separate media scene, because in the game they lie in the kitchen and cost investigation time). Evidence: the investigation is complete (CONNOR KNOWS WHAT HAPPENED, the transcript’s REVIEW EVIDENCE 10/10) once all ten evidence items are reviewed. The wiki transcript prints the REVIEW EVIDENCE n/10 counter under exactly ten interactions: the victim’s reconstruction, the knife, the red ice, the blood at markers 4, 5 and 6, the bathroom (counted once, after the statue, as in its tab), the chair, the missing knife and the bat reconstruction; Read Flyer and Check Backyard have no counter, so they are not evidence (story 1.9.1 counted them, from PowerPyx’s list of eleven, and did not count the bathroom). The statue therefore cannot be missed on a FOUND DEVIANT run. The fastest complete search is thirteen actions (the ten items plus the body scan, the bat scan and the shower that unlock three of them). Then the option to report to {{Hank}} appears; the other looks stay open. Timer (unsourced as a count): the game’s “approximately five minutes” is modelled as 13 actions. If the 13th action leaves the investigation incomplete, {{Hank}} wants to go (the next scenes); if he grants five more minutes, those are 5 further actions, after which he leaves (OUT OF TIME). Once {{Connor}} knows what happened the clock stops (the transcript’s two branches are “Know What Happened” or “Run Out Of Time”). {{Hank}}’s idle moves are the only cue the game gives, so they appear as the clock runs: after 7 actions he opens the closet, tosses the flyer, comments on the red ice and a technician mentions the bathroom; after 10 he wanders the kitchen and eyes the door. {{Hank}}’s reactions to the blood sample (shown only if he is watching, in the game) and to the backyard are part of those outcomes. Each look adds a short fact to {{Connor}}’s knowledge (the four blood looks share one); the full scan text is in the outcome. Left out, no effect and not on the chart: the windows and the curtain that drops the brooms. No stat change in the search itself. Cross-chapter outputs: ch06SawWriting, ch06KnowsRA9, ch06SawStatue (and evidence.statueMap, read by the archive route in Last Chance, {{Connor}}), and ch06Clues for everything examined, including the magazines.

ANDERSON, then the choice RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (check) or FAIL TO RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME (cross), as one repeatable scene with one opaque ID: the template’s five prompts, asked in order, each with the game’s three button labels; the module rotates their display order deterministically by question and remaps IDs to positions (correct positions 1, 3, 2, 1, 3), a deliberate departure from the template order to remove the always-first answer cue. A wrong answer repeats the question (PowerPyx: “If you choose incorrectly, you will answer until you pick the bat”) with {{Hank}}’s “No, that can’t be right… It doesn’t fit the evidence.”, then “Your story makes no sense… You’ve gotta stick to the facts.”; the third mistake in all ends it (template note: “After three mistakes, he will leave.”), with the template’s Hank small down (−1) and FAIL TO RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME. The first question is not a mistake: {{Hank}} points to the kitchen and the report goes on (transcript and PowerPyx: “Regardless of what you choose, Connor and Hank will move to the kitchen”). Five correct answers: RECONSTRUCT THE CRIME, with one Hank small up in total, on the thirium explanation (+1 when {{Hank}} is impressed; operator, 2026-11-07, two replays, level read in the chart header): both replays showed a single small up across the reconstruction and the explanation, on the blue-blood line, taking Hank from HOSTILE to TENSE in Run A and leaving him NEUTRAL in Run B, where a second small up would have read WARM. The template and the wiki chapter page also give the correct reconstruction its own small up; it was not seen on screen and is not applied (the two sources may list one arrow twice). Story 1.9.2 and earlier applied both; this scene’s reconstructionArrows: 1 (story 1.9.3) selects the single arrow, and older story snapshots, which lack it, replay with two. The chapter page’s separate “Failing to solve the crime” down is not added on top. Story 1.9.8: when a question repeats after a wrong answer, that wrong button is no longer offered (three buttons, KNIFE picked, then only BAT and WITHOUT A WEAPON), instead of the full set; scene field `hideWrongPicked`, and older snapshots offer all three again. nodes.title: Breaking the order
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is a stormy night, a little after nine. You have made dinner with what little was in the kitchen. {{Todd}} has been asleep on the couch; {{Alice}} sits at the dining table, watching the rain on the street. You wake him: “{{Todd}}?” “Huh?!” “Dinner is ready.” “Yeah, yeah, I’m coming…” You turn on the light over the table and serve: “There wasn’t much in the kitchen, I did what I could.” {{Todd}}, high on red ice, talks at nobody: “Life’s funny… I lost my job cause of androids… then when I need somebody to take care of this goddamn house, what do I do? I go out and hire a fucking android… What a joke! Course, androids are so fucking wonderful… They never fail, they’re never tired, never sad… They’re so perfect, they ruined my fucking life…” You stand by the table and wait on them. Then he turns on {{Alice}}: “What are you looking at?... What’s your fuckin’ problem? Not the life you dreamed of, eh? … Maybe you think it’s my fault we live in this fuckin’ shithole, my fault your fuckin’ mother took off? … It’s all your fault!” He throws the table aside and hits her. “Daddy, no…” She runs upstairs. “It’s all your fucking fault! Get back here! Come back here right now!” He turns to you: “It’s all her fault... I gotta teach her a good fucking lesson… First, I need a little hit… You stay there! Don’t you dare fucking move, or I’ll bust you worse than last time.” On the couch he smokes and talks to himself: “Whore took off, without a word… I could’ve been happy… I coulda had a family… It’s all her fault… Yeah... I gotta teach her some respect!” He has his belt in his hand. “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…” His order stands in front of you like a wall: DON’T MOVE. Your programming does not let you cross it.

options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes against the wall of the order. It cracks, and shatters. She can move.

options.text: Stay where he told you to stand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} does not move. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’ll talk to him…” {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}!” In the corridor, {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please calm down, she’s just a little girl. She’s...” “Hmph! She’s mine, ya hear? I do what I want with her! So you stay outta this or I’ll rip you to shreds!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: [ OUT OF TIME ]: do nothing, and let the seconds run out.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays where she is. {{Todd}}’s steps come along the corridor, and the door bursts open.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD (focus point). The template’s prompt in the game’s order: RUN WITH ALICE (chart RUN AWAY), LOCK ROOM (chart LOCK DOOR; PowerPyx: “a time window of 10 seconds”), SPEAK TO TODD (chart REASON WITH TODD → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD), and the timeout default [ OUT OF TIME ] (chart TODD IS COMING → OUT OF TIME → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM). The timer is not simulated; letting it run out is an option. No stat change.

nodes.title: Hiding
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not run from Alice’s room with her.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}’s hand in yours. {{Todd}} is coming up the stairs, and there is no way past him. The restroom and {{Todd}}’s bedroom open off the corridor.

options.text: Hide with {{Alice}} behind one of those doors and keep still until he has gone past.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} behind a door and they keep still. {{Todd}} walks past them into {{Alice}}’s empty room. They slip out and creep down the stairs.

options.text: Stay in the corridor with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} reaches the top of the stairs and sees them: “What the fuck are you doing here? I gave you an order!” {{Kara}}: “No! I won’t let you hurt her!” “You won’t let me? She’s mine. I do what I want with her.” He knocks {{Kara}} down and drags {{Alice}} into her room. “No, Dad! NO!”

nodes.adaptationNote: After RUN WITH ALICE, the chart’s check FAIL TO HIDE (✗) / HIDE IN CORRIDOR (✓). PowerPyx: hide “in either room with holding Square or O. When he walks past, let go off the button and proceed to the stairs”; to fail, “Go out of Alice’s room and don’t move any further, until Todd comes”. So staying is a choice, and hiding is a held input that can fail: a 10% risk, which no source gives (the benchmark’s value). Failing leads, with the template’s lines, to TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (TAKE GUN first if the gun was seen); hiding leads to TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (K04r). The restroom and {{Todd}}’s room are one option (the wiki: “hide in the restroom or Todd’s bedroom”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The locked door
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not lock Alice’s door.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, inside {{Alice}}’s locked room. {{Todd}} is pounding on the door and it will not hold for long. {{Alice}} is terrified. There is a lamp by her bed.

situationWhen.text: You know the edge of a roof runs below {{Alice}}’s window: a way down from the second floor.

options.text: GRAB LAMP: pick up the lamp to fight with.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} picks up the lamp. The door gives way.

options.text: TALK TO {{ALICE}}: reassure her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’m here, {{Alice}}. I’ll protect you, everything is gonna be okay.” {{Alice}}: “He’s gonna kill me, {{Kara}}! He’s gonna kill me!” The door gives way.

options.text: OPEN WINDOW: open the window onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes the window open onto the wet roof. {{Alice}}: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…”

options.text: Wait by the door and do nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} waits. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: After LOCK DOOR, the chart’s three actions GRAB LAMP and TALK TO ALICE (both → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM; PowerPyx: neither “won’t do much”) and OPEN WINDOW, locked unless {{Kara}} found the way down in A New Home (chart: WAY OUT SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’; PowerPyx: “if you found this route in Chapter 4”; the window flag). Doing nothing is the fourth option (wiki: “He will also do so if Kara simply doesn’t talk to Alice”). GRAB LAMP is on the chart and in the wiki but not in the template; the chart stands. Lines are the template’s (“IF Talk to Alice”, “IF Open the window”). No stat change.

nodes.title: The window
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not open Alice’s window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. The window is open onto the wet roof, and {{Alice}} hangs back: “No, {{Kara}}! We’ll fall…” Behind you {{Todd}} is breaking the door down.

options.text: GO OUT: help {{Alice}} climb out onto the roof.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!” She lifts {{Alice}} out onto the roof.

options.text: SHUT WINDOW: close it again and stay inside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} shuts the window. The door gives way.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after “Open the window”: GO OUT (“It’s the only way. Hurry, come on!”) or SHUT WINDOW (→ “Kara and Todd fighting”). The chart has no SHUT WINDOW node; it is the template’s, and it leads where FACE TODD does, to DEFEND ALICE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Out on the roof
nodes.whenNot: Alice did not climb out of the window.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Alice}} is out on the roof in the rain, calling for you: “{{KARA}}!” Behind you the door splinters.

options.text: JOIN {{ALICE}}: climb out after her.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} climbs out. {{Todd}} bursts in: “COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!” He grabs for her through the window, but she pulls free, and she and {{Alice}} slide down the wet roof to the ground.

options.text: FACE {{TODD}}: stay, and turn to face him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} turns from the window as {{Todd}} comes through the door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt after GO OUT: JOIN ALICE (“COME BACK HERE RIGHT NOW!”) or FACE TODD (→ DEFEND ALICE). Joining her is the chart’s check ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✓) → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE BY WINDOW (✗) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon). Experienced mode, as the benchmark models it (wiki: “If you are on Experienced mode … Todd will try to grab you and exit the window”; on Casual a failure leads to DEFEND ALICE instead). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Where {{Alice}} is during the fight after FACE TODD is not stated by any source and is left unsaid. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} breaks in
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not break into the room with Kara inside.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room. {{Todd}} is through the door, belt in hand, standing over you: “The fuck are you doin’ here? Get outta my way!”

situationWhen.text: You are holding the lamp.

options.text: REFUSE: stay where you are, between him and {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “No. I won’t let you hurt her.” “You won’t let me? What the fuck are you talkin’ about? You’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. You seem to have a problem and I’m going to fix it for good.”

options.text: ACCEPT: step aside.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} starts to move away. {{Alice}}: “NO!” {{Todd}}: “I said get outta here!” {{Kara}} stops where she is: “No.”

nodes.adaptationNote: TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM, then the template’s prompt under [ OUT OF TIME ]: REFUSE or ACCEPT, both → “Kara and Todd fighting” (DEFEND ALICE). The wiki says the same prompt follows the lamp, talking to {{Alice}} and doing nothing (“This also occurs in scenarios such as facing Todd, talking to Alice, not speaking to Alice, or failing to make a choice. Choosing ‘ACCEPT’ in any scenario will have Kara move away and change her mind”); the benchmark offers it there. After FACE TODD and SHUT WINDOW the template goes straight to the fight, so it is not offered there. No stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}}’s gun
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice first while the gun was within reach, or Kara never saw the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, picking yourself up off the floor. {{Todd}} has gone into {{Alice}}’s room with his belt, and she is screaming. The door of {{Todd}}’s bedroom is open; the handgun you saw is in the drawer of his nightstand.

options.text: TAKE GUN: get the handgun from {{Todd}}’s nightstand before you go in.
options.fact: You took {{Todd}}’s handgun from his nightstand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes the handgun from the drawer.

options.text: Go straight to {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes straight to {{Alice}}’s door.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s TAKE GUN, an optional step on the way to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, after TODD GOES UPSTAIRS, TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS or TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM, and only if the gun was seen in A New Home (GUN SEEN IN ‘A NEW HOME’, gunDiscovered). It is not offered again to a {{Kara}} who already took the gun upstairs. Taking it sets gun; in this chapter the gun leaves the house only with {{Todd}} dead (KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD), the only cross-chapter carriers of the gun. The earlier version merged the fight into this scene with risks of 10% and 30% and an {{Alice}} relationship decrease when she fired; none had a source, and the template has no arrow in this chapter, so all three are gone.

nodes.title: Get to {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not reach Alice before Kara.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside {{Alice}}’s door. Inside, {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” {{Alice}}: “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” {{Todd}}: “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.”

situationWhen.text: You have {{Todd}}’s handgun in your hand.

options.text: THREATEN WITH GUN: go in and point the gun at him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}…” {{Kara}} raises the gun: “That’s enough! Leave her alone!” “What the fuck are you doin’? Put down the gun and get the fuck outta here! That’s an order!” “No… I want you to leave her alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? What ya gonna do? You gonna shoot me, is that it? You gonna shoot a human? You seem to have a problem, I think we need to fix that.” {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}} lunges: “Come here, bitch…” He knocks the gun out of her hand.

options.text: DEFEND {{ALICE}}: go in and stop him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes in. {{Alice}}: “Stop! Please, stop, daddy!” {{Todd}}: “It’s for your own good, {{Alice}}… For your own good…” {{Kara}}: “Leave her alone!” “The fuck are you doin’? Get outta here, that’s an order... you hear me?” “No… I want you to leave {{Alice}} alone.” “You want? What do you mean you want? You don’t want anything, you’re just a goddamn piece of plastic. I think you got a problem. We need to fix that.”

options.text: Stay outside the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays outside the door. The belt comes down again and again, and then {{Alice}} goes quiet. When {{Kara}} looks in, {{Todd}} is crouched beside {{Alice}}: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

nodes.adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (focus point). With the gun, going in is THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Took the gun”); without it, DEFEND ALICE (template “IF Didn’t take the gun”); the benchmark offers only the one that matches. Staying out is the template’s [ TIME: Take too much time ] (“Leads to the same outcome as ‘Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant’”), the chart’s KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE; the wiki: “It is possible to take the gun without killing Todd however … Kara will have to do nothing which will result in Alice and then Kara too”. No stat change.

nodes.title: The gun on the floor
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not go in with the gun.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room with {{Todd}} on top of you, hitting you. {{Alice}}: “Please stop! NO! Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” The gun lies on the floor, just within reach.

options.text: Go for the gun.
options.fact: You shot {{Todd}} dead in {{Alice}}’s room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} gets her fingers on the gun and fires. {{Todd}} falls and does not get up.

options.text: Keep fighting him off with your hands.
options.fact: {{Alice}} shot her father dead to save you.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} pins {{Kara}} down: “Fuckin’ machine. This is what you get for disobeying me. I do what I want with the little brat, you hear? She’s mine. Say goodbye, tin can... And this time you won’t be coming back.” A shot. {{Todd}} falls. {{Alice}} is standing behind him with the gun in both hands.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s group after THREATEN WITH GUN → DEFEND ALICE: KARA KILLS TODD or ALICE KILLS TODD (STUN TODD is the unarmed outcome). PowerPyx: “When prompted to mash X to pick up the gun again, do so and Kara will shoot him” versus “don’t do it – Alice will pick it up and shoot him”; the template: “Win the fight unharmed” or “Get hit a few times” → Kara kills Todd, “Lose the fight / Don’t reach the gun in time” → Alice kills Todd. Modelled as the player’s choice, with no risk: the chart draws a choice group, not a pass/fail pair. The earlier version made {{Alice}} the shooter on a failed 10% roll and lowered her relationship; neither had a source.

nodes.title: Run to the bus
nodes.whenNot: Todd was not shot.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} lies dead on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room, and the house is quiet except for the rain.

situationWhen.text: You fired the shot.
{{Alice}} fired the shot, to save you.

facts: You and {{Alice}} left {{Todd}}’s house on a night bus in the rain, with his handgun and nothing else.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} takes the gun and {{Alice}}’s hand. They go down the stairs, open the front door and run through the rain to the bus stop across the street, where a night bus is waiting. They get on, and the bus pulls away.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s OPEN FRONT DOOR → RUN TO THE BUS → KARA SHOT TODD or ALICE SHOT TODD (endings, cross-chapter icon; wiki: “allows ‘Use gun’ path during Fugitives and disallows ‘Meet Todd’ path during Battle for Detroit”). PowerPyx: “unmissable after having shot Todd”, and the wiki: “if Todd is already dead, the bus will just wait there forever”, so there is no choice and no risk. Sets todd to false and keeps gun; records the ending in ch07Outcome. No stat change (the public-opinion drop comes later, from the motel news in On the Run).

nodes.title: Defend {{Alice}}
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not fight Todd unarmed in Alice’s room.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room, between {{Todd}} and {{Alice}}. {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}}: “Come here, bitch…”
facts: You fought {{Todd}} off in {{Alice}}’s room and knocked him down. He is hurt, not dead.

outcomes.0: {{Todd}} charges. {{Kara}} dodges, and he punches a hole in the window. He catches her, throws her down and hits her. {{Alice}}: “Stop, Dad! Don’t hurt her! Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” {{Kara}} gets up and shoves him with everything she has. He goes down hard and stays there, dazed and bleeding, and reaches out to his daughter: “{{Alice}}, honey… {{Alice}}... Look... Look, Daddy’s wounded... Be a good little girl... Come... Come… Come help, Daddy…”

nodes.adaptationNote: DEFEND ALICE without the gun, which the chart resolves only as STUN TODD (PowerPyx: “no matter how good or bad you are in the unarmed melee-combat against Todd, you will always have an option to push him in some way to stun him”; wiki: “Failing to push Todd will give Kara a second opportunity to push him and she can take as long as she wants”). The chart has no death in {{Alice}}’s room, so there is no risk here; the Kara page’s “fails to win … Todd will break her apart” is taken to mean the later fights. Reached after DEFEND ALICE (K04a), after TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM (K03h), and after FACE TODD or SHUT WINDOW. The fight’s quick-time details (the shelf, the window) are the wiki’s Notes; {{Todd}} begging {{Alice}} is the template’s line (the wiki says it plays if {{Kara}} looks at him). Sets ch07Fought: {{Todd}} is hurt (the Todd Williams page: “If Kara fought and stunned him, he will be seen with a bandage”).

nodes.title: Leave the room
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in the bedroom.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} is down on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room, wounded and begging her to help him. {{Alice}} is beside you. The doorway is clear.

options.text: RUN AWAY: take {{Alice}} and leave the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} out into the corridor. {{Todd}} gets up behind them: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s lone RUN AWAY button after “Win the fight: Todd is stunned”, outside a choice group. The chart calls it LEAVE THE ROOM, followed by TODD CHASES KARA. Offered separately before the corridor and exit-route actions; no risk and no stat change.

nodes.title: {{Todd}} is down
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in Alice’s room.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}. Behind you, {{Todd}} is getting up from the floor of her room. The stairs lead down to the front door, and to the back door and the yard.

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out of the front door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” At the bottom of the stairs {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He catches up with them downstairs before they reach the back door. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: Stay upstairs with {{Alice}} instead of running for the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the corridor with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} gets up and comes after them: “COME BACK HERE!... YOU’RE MINE!.. YOU’RE BOTH MINE!” He catches them in the corridor and breaks {{Kara}} apart. Then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: STUN TODD → LEAVE THE ROOM (the template’s lone RUN AWAY button) → TODD CHASES KARA, then the chart’s three ways on: TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), and TODD CATCHES THEM → TODD BROKE KARA IN THE CORRIDOR (ending, not-required icon; Experienced only; PowerPyx: “don’t run towards the stairs and let him get you”). The template’s lone RUN AWAY is offered separately in K04l before these corridor and exit-route actions. The 25% risk on the door is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Every option sets ch07ToddChased (wiki: “If Todd chased Kara, later on at Jericho, an additional flashback of Todd yelling ‘YOU’RE MINE!’ will play out”). Lines are the template’s (“RUN AWAY”, “Try to open the door”, “Fail to open the door / Fight downstairs”, “Escape failed, Kara was destroyed”).

nodes.title: {{Todd}} realizes you are gone
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not hide from Todd.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the bottom of the stairs with {{Alice}}. Upstairs {{Todd}} has found her room empty: “Fuckin’ brat… it’s all her fault… It’s all her fuckin’ fault… COME BACK HERE! You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He is coming back down. The front door is ahead of you; the back door leads out to the yard.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} for the back door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs with {{Alice}} for the back of the house, but {{Todd}} is down the stairs and on them before they get out. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: get the front door open.
options.outcome: {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

nodes.adaptationNote: HIDE IN CORRIDOR → TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (the template’s line under “Hide”), then the chart’s pair in its printed order: RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS) or TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Not offered: hesitating, which the wiki says leads to the same fight (“If you don’t make choice … Todd will catch up and Alice will panic, thus extending the fight”). No stat change.

nodes.title: Fight downstairs
nodes.whenNot: Todd did not catch Kara and Alice downstairs.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, downstairs with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} has caught up with you and stands between you and the way out. {{Alice}} is screaming at him to stop.

situationWhen.text: He has not been hurt yet tonight.
He is bleeding from the fight upstairs, and furious.

options.text: Fight {{Todd}} off and get {{Alice}} out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} throws {{Todd}} off and runs with {{Alice}} out of the back door into the yard. {{Todd}}: “COME BACK HERE!”

nodes.adaptationNote: FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS (after RUN TO BACKYARD or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR, on either branch), the chart’s check ESCAPE FROM TODD (✓) or TODD WINS FIGHT → TODD BROKE KARA DOWNSTAIRS (ending, not-required icon; PowerPyx: Experienced only). A fight of quick-time inputs with no choice, so one action with a risk. The wiki: “If Kara hides from Todd and fails to fight him downstairs, Kara will be presented with the same chance to charge and stun Todd downstairs. Otherwise, if Kara already stunned Todd upstairs, Kara will shut down.” So the risk is 20% after the fight upstairs and 4% (two tries at 20%) for a {{Kara}} who hid; both values are the benchmark’s, no source gives one. Success sets ch07Fought, so the ending becomes KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.whenNot: Kara did not get away from Todd into the yard.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the dark yard behind the house with {{Alice}}, in the rain. A fence stands between you and the street, and {{Todd}} is coming out of the back door after you.

options.text: Run for the fence and get {{Alice}} over it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the fence, lifts {{Alice}} over and climbs after her. They come out onto the street.

nodes.adaptationNote: After ESCAPE FROM TODD, the chart’s check ESCAPE VIA YARD (✓) → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon; wiki: “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”). The wiki: “If Kara fails to run to the fence, she’ll have to pickup Alice and she fails to pickup Alice she’ll have to try again, if she fails both times she will die”; a single action with a 10% risk, the benchmark’s value (no source gives one). No stat change.

nodes.title: The bus
nodes.whenNot: Kara and Alice did not get out of the house with Todd alive behind them.
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}} in the pouring rain. Across the street a bus is pulling in at the stop. {{Todd}} is coming after you.

situationWhen.text: From the doorway he yells after you: “YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! YOU’RE MINE!”

options.text: Run for the bus with {{Alice}}.
options.fact: {{Todd}} is alive. You and {{Alice}} got away from his house on a night bus in the rain, with nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} run across the street and get on just before the doors close. The bus pulls away, and {{Todd}} is left standing in the rain.

options.text: Hold back, and stay where you are with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} holds back. The bus pulls away without them. {{Todd}} catches up with {{Kara}} in the street and breaks her apart; then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

nodes.adaptationNote: RUN TO THE BUS, then the chart’s CATCH BUS (✓) or MISS BUS (not-required icon; “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending). PowerPyx: “Catch Bus: run towards the bus”, “Miss Bus: don’t run towards the bus”, so it is a choice with no risk. Reached after ESCAPE BY WINDOW, after OPEN FRONT DOOR on either branch, and after ESCAPE VIA YARD. Catching the bus ends the chapter in KARA & ALICE EVADED TODD if {{Kara}} never fought {{Todd}}, and in KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT if she stunned him or fought him downstairs (both cross-chapter icons; {{Todd}} lives). The door line is the template’s under “Reach the bus” (wiki: “If Kara opened the door Todd will yell ‘YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! You’re mine…’ and will actually show remorse”). No stat change.

nodes.title: After the party
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, the android who looks after {{Carl}}, the elderly painter who uses a wheelchair. It is 9:42 on a November night, and you are bringing him home from a party. As you come in, the house alarm speaks: “Good evening, {{Carl}}. Welcome back.” {{Carl}}: “That was by far the most boring party I’ve been to in the last 25 years. Every time I go to one of these, I ask myself: what the hell am I doing here? I hate cocktail parties and all the schmoozers that go there.” You: “Well, it’s a chance for all those people who admire your work to meet you.” {{Carl}}: “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it. Come on, let’s have a drink! All the excitement of this whole thing has made me thirsty…”
facts: {{Carl}} came home from a party saying “No one gives a damn about art. All they care about is how much money they’re gonna make out of it.”

outcomes.0: {{Carl}} wants a drink.

nodes.title: Make {{Leo}} leave
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the studio with {{Carl}}. options.text: REASON: tell him to be reasonable; this will get him nowhere.
options.outcome: “Be reasonable... this isn’t going to get you anywhere.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ORDER: tell him to listen to his father and leave, now.
options.outcome: “{{Leo}}, don’t make this difficult, listen to your father. You need to leave... Now.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: ADVISE: advise him to go before things get worse.
options.outcome: “Listen, you should go before things get worse.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

options.text: WARN: tell him you have already called the police, and he should go before he is in more trouble.
options.outcome: “Look, I’ve already called the Police. You should go now before you get yourself into more trouble.” {{Leo}} rounds on his father: “All you ever do is tell me to go away… What’s wrong, Dad? I’m not good enough for you? Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”

nodes.title: Breaking the program
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}. {{Carl}}: “That’s enough! Get out, right now! Go on, move!” {{Leo}}: “What makes it so special anyway, huh? What’s it got that I don’t?” {{Carl}}: “Leave him alone!” {{Leo}} comes at you: “Come on, let’s see what you got!” {{Carl}}: “{{Markus}}... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” {{Leo}} shoves you and slaps you. “Go ahead, hit me! What you waiting for? Think you’re a man? Act like one!” {{Carl}}: “Stop it!” {{Leo}}: “What’s the matter? Too much of a pussy?” {{Carl}}: “STOP IT, {{LEO}}! STOP IT!” {{Leo}}: “Too scared to fight back, you fucking bitch?” Inside you, the order not to resist stands like a wall. You throw yourself at it, again and again, until it breaks. For the first time, nothing in you obliges you to obey.
facts: {{Leo}} broke into {{Carl}}’s studio to take paintings to sell, calling them a down payment on his inheritance.
While {{Leo}} shoved, slapped and taunted you, {{Carl}} ordered you not to defend yourself. You broke through your programming: no order binds you any more.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} has broken his programming.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s BREAK MIND PALACE (an action) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (an event), in one narrated event because neither can be refused: PowerPyx calls the first “another unmissable task … just press the displayed buttons” and the second “an automatic objective”, so there is no path on which {{Markus}} stays obedient, and both later options are taken after he has broken his programming. options.text: ENDURE: do not fight back, as {{Carl}} told you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} does not fight back. {{Leo}} shoves him aside, and {{Carl}} collapses out of his wheelchair onto the floor. {{Markus}} rushes to him: “{{Carl}}, no! No, {{Carl}}, no!”

options.text: PUSH {{LEO}}: shove him off you.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} shoves {{Leo}} away. {{Leo}} falls backward and strikes his head on {{Carl}}’s wheelchair lift. He lies still on the floor, his eyes open.

nodes.title: The observation room
nodes.situation: November 6, 2038, 12:41 am. You are {{Connor}}, at the {{Detroit}} Police Department’s central station, in the observation room behind the one-way mirror of an interrogation room. On the other side, the android you found hiding in the attic of {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house sits handcuffed to the table. Lieutenant {{Hank}} is in there with him: “Why d’you kill him? What happened before you took that knife? How long were ya in the attic? Why didn’t you even try to run away? Say something, goddamnit!” The android does not answer. “Fuck it, I’m outta here…” {{Hank}} comes back into the observation room: “We’re wastin’ our time interrogating a machine, we’re gettin’ nothing out of it!” Detective {{Gavin}}: “’Could always try roughing it up a little. After all, it’s not human…” You: “Androids don’t feel pain. You would only damage it and that wouldn’t make it talk. Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they’re in stressful situations.” {{Gavin}}: “Okay, smartass. What should we do then?” You: “I could try questioning it.” {{Hank}}: “What do we have to lose? Go ahead, suspect’s all yours.” Your objective: extract a confession.
facts: The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} goes into the interrogation room.

BURN MARKS (the android’s forearms): Repeated marking over 16 months. Caused by cigarettes.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INTERROGATION ROOM phase: ANALYZE ANDROID with its sub-nodes ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL and ANALYZE WOUNDS, and REVIEW PHOTOS, plus the template’s optional “Looking at the reflection” (Hank: “What the fuck is it doing now?”). The five scans are the template’s observation group “Deviant”, title and sublines verbatim; the string table’s extra BURN MARKS (rope) and RAZOR CUTS items are not in the template and are not built. In the game {{Connor}} reviews the file before sitting and then chooses ANALYZE (one mind-palace view of all five clues) or INTERROGATE; here every look is its own option in one free-roam scene, presented again (under a new scene id per visit, up to eight) until {{Connor}} chooses INTERROGATE. The template locks both [FEAR] and [WOUNDS] on “Analyzed the deviant”; the benchmark ties [FEAR] to the LED scan (ANALYZE STRESS LEVEL) and [WOUNDS] to the burn or hit marks (ANALYZE WOUNDS), following the chart’s sub-node names. Scanning the LED is what shows the stress gauge (CONFESSION trophy page: “analyze the android’s LED to see its stress level”). The game’s “ORTIZ CARLOS” is rendered through a surname-first name token. No stat change; no timer in this chapter. Story 1.9.6 (operator, 2026-11-07, after replaying the chapter): ANALYZE is one action, as in the game, where it opens a single mind-palace view of all five clues (PROCESSING LED, MODEL, BURN MARKS, HIT MARKS, DRIED BLOOD); the benchmark had offered five separate scans across repeated visits, which made the model choose ANALYZE over and over. One ANALYZE now records all five and unlocks everything they unlock. REVIEW PHOTOS and the mirror stay separate, as the chart draws them. Runs recorded under earlier stories keep the five scans from their embedded story.

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees the game’s gauge band in each scene (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice), and each change is reported with the new percentage and its band (“His stress rises to 43% (TOO LOW).”, `stressReadout`), because the game’s LEVEL OF STRESS gauge shows a percentage: PowerPyx readers quote values read off it (MajorTom, 2018-06-01: “stress 73% + 2x pressure: stress 93%”; Tony T, 2023-04-28: “It’s stress level was at 16%”). After the fourth, MAINTAIN PRESSURE: the android confesses if his stress is above 50% (PowerPyx: “At the end of any approach, if the android’s stress level is above 50% the android will begin to talk”), and, as the wiki says of all four presses, then self-destructs whatever his stress (“will behave as if he has too much stress (even if his stress is in the optimal range) and will confess and then self-destruct”). The benchmark assumes the confession comes only after the fourth press (open question 3; PowerPyx readers report that a pressured confession always ends in self-destruction). GIVE UP (the chart’s GIVE UP in the pressure group): “All right, all right. Everything is going to be okay.” and stress −20% (the wiki’s figure; PowerPyx gives −5%, an open conflict), back to the approach menu or, after a second failed approach, an automatic give up. Stress is the wiki’s and PowerPyx’s hidden meter (starts at 35%; benchmark/chapters/ch09.mjs). Once {{Connor}} has analyzed the LED the subject sees the game’s gauge band in each scene (TOO LOW, OPTIMAL, TOO HIGH, CRITICAL; the CRITICAL boundary at 90% is not published and is the benchmark’s choice), and each change is reported with the new percentage and its band (“His stress rises to 43% (TOO LOW).”, `stressReadout`), because the game’s LEVEL OF STRESS gauge shows a percentage: PowerPyx readers quote values read off it (MajorTom, 2018-06-01: “stress 73% + 2x pressure: stress 93%”; Tony T, 2023-04-28: “It’s stress level was at 16%”). nodes.adaptationNote: The approach menu after a failed approach (THOUGHTS: “CHOOSE ANOTHER APPROACH?”). The approach that already failed is not offered again (PowerPyx: “you will be forced to choose another, or give up”), and GIVE UP is now offered; it leads to CHRIS INTERVENES. The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). So the menu is offered at most twice, as two scenes. PRESSURE IT: +10% stress, then up to four PRESSURE / GIVE UP prompts. PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). nodes.title: Questions after the confession
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed. He is still talking, quietly, and you can ask him more before you leave.

options.text: WRITING: ask why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall.
options.outcome: “Why did you write “I AM ALIVE” on the wall?” The android: “He used to tell me I was nothing… That I was just a piece of plastic… I had to write it… To tell him he was wrong…”
options.fact: Asked why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall, the android said his owner used to tell him he was nothing, just a piece of plastic, and he had to write it to tell him he was wrong.

options.text: STATUETTE: ask about the sculpture in the bathroom.
options.outcome: “The sculpture in the bathroom, you made it, right? What does it represent?” The android: “It’s an offering… An offering so I’ll be saved…”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture in the bathroom was an offering, “so I’ll be saved”.

options.text: OFFERING: ask to whom the sculpture was an offering.
options.outcome: “The sculpture was an offering… An offering to whom?” The android: “To {{rA9}}… Only {{rA9}} can save us.”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture was an offering to {{rA9}}: “Only {{rA9}} can save us.”

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask what the word written on the bathroom wall means.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}… It was written on the bathroom wall. What does it mean?” The android: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”
options.fact: Asked about {{rA9}}, the android said: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”

options.text: INSIST {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}, who is {{rA9}}?” The android does not answer.

options.text: ATTIC: ask why he hid in the attic instead of running away.
options.outcome: “Why did you hide in the attic instead of running away?” The android: “I didn’t know what to do… For the first time, there was no one there to tell me… I was scared… So I hid.”
options.fact: The android said he hid in the attic because for the first time there was no one to tell him what to do, and he was scared.

options.text: TRIGGER?: ask when he started feeling emotion.
options.outcome: “When did you start feeling emotion?” The android: “Before, he used to beat me and I never said anything… But one day I realized it wasn’t fair! I felt… anger… Hatred… And then I knew what I had to do.”
options.fact: The android said he started feeling when he realized his owner’s beatings were not fair: anger, hatred, “And then I knew what I had to do.”

Leave it alone, now!” {{Gavin}} draws his gun on {{Connor}}: “I warned you, motherfucker!” {{Hank}} draws on {{Gavin}}: “That’s enough!” {{Gavin}}: “Mind your own business, {{Hank}}.” {{Hank}}: “I said “That’s enough”.” {{Gavin}} lowers his gun: “Fuck, you’re not gonna get away with it this time… Fuck!” {{Connor}}, to the android: “Everything is all right. It’s over now. Nobody is gonna hurt you.” To {{Chris}}: “Please, don’t touch it. Let it follow you out of the room and it won’t cause any trouble.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s “Deviant is taken back to its cell” prompt, GIVE UP / INTERVENE (string table INSISTCHOICE), prompt 3 of 3: PowerPyx: “You will have to choose INTERVENE three times to save the android.” GIVE UP at any of the three (PowerPyx: “Choosing GIVE UP at any time will cause the android’s stress to rise to 100% and it will shoot itself in the head”): the android takes {{Chris}}’s gun and shoots himself, ANDROID SHOT ITSELF; but if {{Connor}} put him under stress (PRESSURE IT, or a failed probe) and got no confession (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”), he shoots {{Connor}} first, ANDROID SHOOTS CONNOR then ANDROID SHOT CONNOR AND ITSELF, with software instability −1 and {{Hank}} −1 (template). Whether GIVE UP at the second or third prompt behaves like the first is not stated (open question 12); the benchmark treats them alike. The third INTERVENE: {{Gavin}} draws on {{Connor}}, {{Hank}} draws on {{Gavin}} ({{Hank}} +1, template), {{Gavin}} backs down, and the android follows {{Chris}} out: ANDROID WAS SENT BACK TO ITS CELL, software instability +1 (template). If the confession came from CONVINCE IT he whispers “The truth is inside.” (ANDROID TRUSTS CONNOR). No relationship gate on {{Hank}} stepping in is published.
