nodes.title: In the elevator
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. At the food truck you told {{Hank}}: “I just got a report of a suspected deviant. It’s a few blocks away. We should go have a look. I’ll let you finish your meal. I’ll be in the car, if you need me.” Now you stand in the elevator of a run-down building with your eyes closed. {{Hank}}, from the corridor: “Hey {{Connor}}! You ran outta batteries or what?” You: “I’m sorry, I was making a report to {{CyberLife}}.” {{Hank}}: “Uh... Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?” “No! I’m coming.” {{Hank}}: “What do we know about this guy?” You: “Not much. Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor. Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.” {{Hank}}: “Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops. Hey, were you really makin’ a report back there in the elevator? Just by closing your eyes?” “Correct.” “Shit... Wish I could do that…”
facts: A neighbor reported strange noises from a floor of this building where nobody is supposed to live, and a man hiding an LED under his cap.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} follows {{Hank}} down the corridor.

nodes.adaptationNote: {{Connor}}’s closing line at the truck (the template places it after both lunch variants, so it plays on every path), then the chart’s checkpoint IN THE ELEVATOR and the corridor conversation, every line the template’s. No stat change.

nodes.title: Into the nest
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, at the apartment door with {{Hank}}. You knock. No answer. You knock again: “Anybody home? Open up! {{Detroit}} Police!” There is a noise inside. {{Hank}}: “Stay behind me.” “Got it.” He kicks the door in. The apartment is dark, filthy and full of pigeons. {{Hank}}: “What the fuck is this?! Jesus, this place stinks… Uh, looks like we came for nothin’, our man’s gone…”
facts: The apartment the suspect has been living in is full of pigeons. When {{Hank}} kicked the door in, nobody was in sight.

outcomes.0: Your objective: INVESTIGATE THE APARTMENT.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s INTO THE NEST: knock twice, {{Hank}} kicks the door in (PowerPyx; the template’s “Knocking on the door”, every line the template’s). The noise inside is from the wiki’s Hank page (“will hear noises from within the room”); the pigeons from the Rupert page (“It was full of pigeons”). The objective is the HUD string THOUGHTS.0501C.INVESTIGATE. No stat change.

nodes.title: Magazines in the first room
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, just inside the apartment. In the first room to the right of the door, before the room with the birds, two magazines lie on a table. Reading takes time, and {{Hank}} will not wait long.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Red Ice Epidemic
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that red ice has become the drug of choice for the city’s growing underclass; analysts suggest it flourishes on the dissatisfaction caused by androids taking human jobs. The main ingredient of android blue blood is among its active agents; the dealers’ motto is “Where the blood is blue, the ice is red... and the money is green”.

media.title: Green Earth: Past the Tipping Point
facts: Green Earth reports that scientists say the planet has officially passed its environmental tipping point: rainforests reduced by 79% since 2000 and coastal corals by 58%, too much carbon in the atmosphere for the environment ever to absorb, and natural resources almost exhausted. “The planet will keep getting hotter now. The only question is, how fast?”

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “RED ICE EPIDEMIC” and READ “PAST THE TIPPING POINT”, in that order: the two magazines in the first room to the right of the door (PowerPyx), as a media scene: read either, both or neither. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s article pages; interviewees are not named. In the game they can be read at any time during the search; here they come first, and each magazine read counts as one action of the search’s time budget (see C10o1). Neither changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Replaces the earlier wording, which called the drug’s users unemployed and the room a squat.

nodes.title: Investigate the apartment
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, searching the apartment with {{Hank}}, among the pigeons. In the main room: a poster on the wall, a military jacket, a driver’s license, a bird cage lying on the floor, a chair, a pack of birdseed, a refrigerator and a closet. In the bathroom: the sink, and a wall covered in writing above an overturned stool. Each thing you examine takes time, and {{Hank}} is in no mood to stay. What do you do?

options.outcome: DRIVER’S LICENSE | Name: {{Rupert}} {{Travis}} | Authenticity: Forgery. SUSPECT USED FORGED ID. You: “The driver’s license is fake.” {{Hank}}: “Cool! At least we didn’t come for nothing…”

options.outcome: BLUE BLOOD | MODEL WB200 #847 004 961 | Reported Missing - 10/11/2036. LED | Biocomponent #9301 | Deactivated: 11/06/2038 - 11:36. You: “Its LED is in the sink.” {{Hank}}: “Not surprised it was an android. No human could live with all these fuckin’ pigeons…” SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT.

options.text: Examine the bird cage on the floor of the main room.
options.fact: By the bird cage in the main room: SKID MARK - RECENT, trail width 19.6 inches, traces of galvanized steel; FINGER MARKS - RECENT, traces of avian fecal matter, no fingerprints; METAL HOOK, recently broken, 100% stainless steel.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ INVESTIGATE APARTMENT ] as a free search, one action per visit, each once: every clue in the template’s order with the game’s observation text (the poster and its corner, the diary behind it, the jacket, the driver’s license, the sink’s LED and blue blood, the rA9 writing, the stool and its marker pen, the bird cage’s three clues), the two reconstructions PowerPyx describes, the chair (FIND RUPERT), and the wiki’s incidental items (birdseed, the empty refrigerator, the pigeon closet). The HUD conclusions are the game’s THOUGHTS.0501C strings (SUSPECT USED FORGED ID, SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT, OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE WRITING, SUSPECT HEARD US ENTER, SUSPECT RAN TO THE LIVING ROOM, SUSPECT IS STILL HERE, SUSPECT CARES FOR WILD ANIMALS, SUSPECT DOESN’T EAT; once the sink is examined the game reads DEVIANT for SUSPECT on the forged ID, the birdseed and the refrigerator, and so does the benchmark). Chart nodes: SEE RA9 REFERENCE (the writing), INVESTIGATE STOOL (the stool; the chart hangs it off the writing, so it needs the writing first), INVESTIGATE CAGE, FIND LED (the sink), FIND DIARY (the poster, then pulling it off; cross-chapter), FIND RUPERT (the chair, which needs the cage reconstruction: PowerPyx, “Compete the reconstruction to determine that the android has climbed up into the ceiling”). Whether the stool reconstruction or the LED is also required is not published (research note, open question 1); here only the cage reconstruction is. The reconstructions’ wording is the benchmark’s summary of PowerPyx and the HUD strings. The timer (wiki Connor page: “if he cannot deduce the deviant’s location in time, Hank calls off the search”; PowerPyx: “about five minutes”) is an action budget: eight actions, each magazine read counting as one, before {{Hank}} wants to leave (STAY / LEAVE within C10o1), and three more if {{Connor}} asks for the two minutes. These counts are the benchmark’s, not published. {{Hank}}’s own lines are the template’s and play as time passes: the bookshelf after two actions, the sink prompt after four if {{Connor}} has not looked, the jacket after five if he has not examined it, the window after six. The rA9 line names {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android only if {{Connor}} checked the shower in Partners (string pair SHOWERCLUE / SHOWERCLUENO), read from a chapter 6 flag if one exists, otherwise the second line. No stat change anywhere in the search (template, wiki). One repeatable hub retains its scene ID across all examinations; STAY / LEAVE replaces the examination menu at eight actions in the same hub. The chapter availability hook prepares state-dependent outcomes and sets for the generic clue hub. Story 1.9.7: the rA9 wall’s line reads “the same sign {{Ortiz}}’s android wrote” (surname only), as the game’s SHOWERCLUE does (X0502C.LIVING.INSCRIPTIONS.PC.X05CCONNOR.SHOWERCLUE.3); the first name was an addition. Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, yjqf4mP0tVA 28:07.

Waiting instead of running is the wiki’s first LOSE SIGHT OF RUPERT route (“If Connor waits before opening the door when Rupert runs, Connor will open the door and find that Rupert is gone”), which ends the chapter at RUPERT GOT AWAY with the template’s lose-sight lines (variant “Lose Rupert”, no arrow). How the twelve previews group into forks, which fork holds which death, and every probability (8%, 10%, 13%) are the benchmark’s; no source gives them (research note, open question 10). Non-fatal stumbles (the cart, the train tumble, the ladder pull-up) are not modelled. Once {{Connor}} loses the deviant or dies, the remaining forks do not play.

nodes.title: The deviant pushes {{Hank}}
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, gaining on the deviant across a rooftop of the farm. {{Hank}} has taken a separate route and gets to him first: “STOP RIGHT THERE!” The deviant shoves him. {{Hank}} goes over the edge of the roof and catches it with his hands; he is hanging there, several stories up. outcomes.0: Your analysis of {{Hank}}: CHANCE OF SURVIVAL: 89%.

nodes.title: {{Hank}} on the ledge
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Hank}} is hanging from the edge of the roof by his hands. Your analysis: CHANCE OF SURVIVAL: 89%. The deviant is getting away across the roofs. You have only a moment.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: leave {{Hank}} and go after the deviant.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs on and corners the deviant at the edge of a roof. The deviant: “Please, I’ve done nothing wrong… I just wanted to be free. You know what they’ll do to me if you turn me in…” You: “Model 874 004 961, serious malfunctions have been detected in your software, including Class 4 errors. You’ve been deemed defective and will be sent back to {{CyberLife}} for deactivation.” {{Hank}}, who has pulled himself up, catches up and slaps you: “Don’t you fucking move! You bastard! You saw I was gonna fall and you’d rather let me die than fail your fucking mission!” You: “I had to make a choice... It seemed to me…” {{Hank}}: “What am I to you? A statistic? A “zero”, a “one” in your fucking program? Uh? Is that how you see humans, you bastard?! Jesus!” You: “I understand you’re upset… Perhaps I didn’t assess th-” {{Hank}}: “Fuck you and your fuckin assessment! Come here.” He cuffs the deviant. The deviant: “Why are you doing this?” {{Hank}}: “Alright, shut up!” The deviant, to you: “You’re one of us! You’re helping humans… But you’re just their slave!” {{Hank}}: “I said shut up! Alright. Come along!” The deviant: “{{RA9}}, save me.” He tears free and throws himself off the roof. {{Hank}}: “Hey! What the f- Holy shit…”

options.text: SAVE {{HANK}}: pull {{Hank}} back up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} pulls {{Hank}} back onto the roof. The deviant is gone. {{Hank}}: “Shit! Oh SHIT! We had it! FUCK!” You: “It’s my fault, I should have been faster.” {{Hank}}: “You’d have caught it if it weren’t for me… That’s alright. We know what it looks like. We’ll find it… Hey, {{Connor}}… Nothing.”

options.text: Press neither: hesitate until the moment passes.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} stays where he is until the moment has passed, then runs on after the deviant.

nodes.title: Inside {{Jericho}}
nodes.situation: November 6th, 2038, 5:13 pm. You are {{Markus}}. You have found {{Jericho}}: the dark hold of an old ship, where androids who ran from their owners hide. Some huddle by fires; many are damaged. You are wounded in the abdomen and losing blue blood. Three androids stand in front of you, and one of them has just said: “Welcome to {{Jericho}}.” You ask: “Who are you?” “Fugitives… just like you... My name is {{Josh}}.” “I’m {{Simon}}.” A young woman: “{{North}}.”
facts: {{Jericho}} is the hold of an old ship where androids who escaped their owners hide. There you met {{Josh}}, {{Simon}} and {{North}}.

outcomes.0: {{Markus}} looks from one to the other.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE JERICHO (no choice), with the template’s opening lines of the section “In Jericho” (date and time NOV 6TH, 2038, PM 05:13; “Who are you?”; the three introductions). The template continues from the previous chapter’s last line, Simon’s “Welcome to Jericho.”, which is quoted here without naming the speaker. The abdominal wound is the one Lucy treats later (the wiki: “Markus’ injury on his abdomen”; PowerPyx: “She will heal Markus’s wounds”); how he got it belongs to the previous chapter and is not narrated. The two prompts that follow use the game’s Jericho script prefix (X0503M) but the template places them here, at the start of this chapter. No stat change.

nodes.title: Who they are
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hold of {{Jericho}} with {{Josh}}, {{Simon}} and {{North}}, who have just told you their names. What do you say to them?

options.text: TRAIL: say that they knew only an android could follow the trail.
options.outcome: “And you knew that only an android could follow the trail, didn’t you?” {{Josh}}: “Only those who are like us can find {{Jericho}}…” {{Simon}}: “If you could decipher the signs, it’s because one of us trusted you enough to give you the key.”

options.text: ANDROID: ask how many of them there are.
options.fact: {{North}} told you there are nineteen androids in {{Jericho}} still in working order; the rest were damaged escaping their masters.
options.outcome: “How many are you?” {{North}}: “There are nineteen of us still in working order... The rest were damaged escaping their masters...” {{Josh}}: “Many tried to reach {{Jericho}}... Few succeed... Humans have little pity for our kind…”

options.text: {{JERICHO}}: ask whether this is {{Jericho}}.
options.outcome: “This is {{Jericho}}?” {{Josh}}: “It’s a refuge for those who don’t want to be slaves anymore...”

options.text: REFUGE: say you thought {{Jericho}} was a place where androids lived in freedom.
options.outcome: “I don’t understand… I thought {{Jericho}} was a place where androids lived in freedom...” {{Josh}}: “We do live in freedom… It may not be what you hoped for, but here we have no master. We don’t belong to anybody.”

options.text: FREE?: ask whether hiding just to stay alive is their idea of freedom.
options.outcome: “And hiding just to stay alive… That’s freedom to you?” {{Josh}}: “Humans hate us. Hiding is the only way we can survive.” {{North}}: “There is no safe place for those like us. If humans knew we’re here, they’d kill us.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s first prompt of the arrival (choice group X0503M.JERICHO.ENCOUNTER.PC.CHOICE01), not a chart node: the game’s five buttons in the game’s order (TRAIL, ANDROID, JERICHO, REFUGE, FREE?), each shown as its label then a short description, with the spoken line and the replies, all the template’s, in the outcome. One pick, as the template has a single choice group followed by one common line. No arrow on any option (the template shows none). Phileas’s wiki page says he “may appear in a flashback if Markus mentions the trail”; that flashback is not in the template and is not narrated (research note, open question 5).

nodes.title: More freedom than you ever had
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the hold of {{Jericho}}. {{Josh}}: “I understand how you feel... but we have more freedom here than you ever did.” How do you answer?

options.text: LOST: say you came looking for hope and will not find any here.
options.fact: {{North}} told you to go and see {{Lucy}}: “She may be able to help you.”
options.outcome: “I came to {{Jericho}} looking for hope... Looks like I’m not gonna find any here…” {{Simon}}: “You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now is deal with it.” {{Josh}}: “You’re safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.” {{North}}: “Go and see {{Lucy}}. She may be able to help you.”

options.text: SOMBER: say that maybe you were never really free, and now need to decide who you are.
options.fact: {{North}} told you to go and see {{Lucy}}: “She may be able to help you.”
options.outcome: “Maybe I was never really free... Maybe I was only what my master wanted me to be... And now I need to decide who I really am...” {{Simon}}: “You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now is deal with it.” {{Josh}}: “You’re safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.” {{North}}: “Go and see {{Lucy}}. She may be able to help you.”

options.text: LUCID: say that fear has only become their new master.
options.fact: {{North}} told you to go and see {{Lucy}}: “She may be able to help you.”
options.outcome: “Humans were your masters, and now it’s fear that rules you… You’re no freer than you ever were… You’ve only found a new master.” {{Simon}}: “You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now is deal with it.” {{Josh}}: “You’re safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.” {{North}}: “Go and see {{Lucy}}. She may be able to help you.”

options.text: DIRECT: say that waiting in the dark is not how you see freedom.
options.fact: {{North}} told you to go and see {{Lucy}}: “She may be able to help you.”
options.outcome: “Waiting in the dark for something to happen? That’s not how I see freedom.” {{Simon}}: “You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now is deal with it.” {{Josh}}: “You’re safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.” {{North}}: “Go and see {{Lucy}}. She may be able to help you.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s second prompt of the arrival (CHOICE02), not a chart node: the game’s four buttons in the game’s order (LOST, SOMBER, LUCID, DIRECT), label first, with the spoken line in the outcome. Josh’s line before it and the closing lines of Simon, Josh and North after it are the template’s, the same on every branch. No arrow on any option (the template shows none). North’s pointer to Lucy is added to what Markus knows.

nodes.title: The hold
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, free to walk around the hold of {{Jericho}}. Your objectives: settle in, and explore {{Jericho}}. Damaged androids sit or stand in the gloom. {{Josh}} is by the wall, watching over a small boy android. {{North}} sits on a box, bouncing a ball against a wall. A damaged android sits on the floor. Crates are stacked by the wall. {{Simon}} stands in the middle of the room. You can do one thing at a time, in any order; once you have seen {{Lucy}} and explored the hold, you can go to {{Simon}}.

options.text: Go over to the female android standing near the fire at the side of the hold.
options.fact: A dying android by the fire asked you whether you knew what happens after death. You did not. She said she was glad to meet you, and shut down.
options.outcome: The android looks at {{Markus}}: “I’ve heard humans are afraid of dying too… Do you know what happens after death?” “No… No, I don’t…” “Well, I’m about to find out… What’s your name?” “{{Markus}}.” “I was glad to meet you, {{Markus}}.” She shuts down.

options.text: Go over to {{Josh}} and the boy he is watching over.
options.fact: {{Josh}} told you the boy was thrown out by his owners and lived on the streets. The androids of {{Jericho}} need blue blood and biocomponents; they salvage what they can from those who shut down, but there is never enough: “We’re slowly dying out…”
options.outcome: {{Josh}}: “They threw him out when they didn’t want him anymore... He was living on the streets before we brought him here...” {{Markus}}: “They’ll all shut down if we don’t find a way to help them…” {{Josh}}: “To help them we need blue blood and biocomponents. We salvage what we can from those who shut down… But there’s never enough…” “So… How do they survive?” “They won’t. We’re slowly dying out…”

options.text: Go over to {{North}} and talk to her.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} goes over to {{North}}. She keeps bouncing the ball against the wall.

options.text: Talk to the damaged android sitting on the floor.
options.fact: A damaged android in the hold told you humans tied him to the back of a car “to have fun”. He does not want to shut down.
options.outcome: The android: “I’m not in very good shape, am I?.. My diagnostic program isn’t working... I don’t think it would have anything good to say anyway…” {{Markus}}: “What happened to you?” “They tied me to the back of a car... I think they wanted to have fun... I don’t wanna shut down... No, I... I don’t wanna shut down...”

options.text: Light the four oil drums in the hold.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} lights the oil drums one by one, four in all. Androids drift over and gather around the flames, though none of them needs the warmth.

options.text: Go and see {{Lucy}}, behind the white plastic sheet.
options.fact: {{Lucy}} stopped your bleeding and gave you blue blood to drink. Holding your hand, she said: “You had it all and you lost it all... You’ve seen hell and now hell lives in you... A part of shadow and a part of light... Which will prevail? Your choices will shape our destiny.”
options.outcome: “Are you {{Lucy}}?” {{Lucy}}: “Sit down. Show me…” She looks at the wound. “I’ll stop the bleeding.” She treats it and hands him blue blood. “Drink this.” Then: “Give me your hand.” She holds it. “You had it all and you lost it all... You’ve seen hell and now hell lives in you... Your heart is troubled… A part of shadow and a part of light... Which will prevail? Your choices will shape our destiny.”

options.text: Check the crates by the wall.
options.fact: An empty {{CyberLife}} crate in the hold told you where parts come from: the {{CyberLife}} warehouses in {{Detroit}} Harbor, which hold everything {{Jericho}} needs.
options.outcome: Among the crates by the wall {{Markus}} finds an empty {{CyberLife}} shipping crate. Parts like the ones {{Jericho}} lacks are shipped from the {{CyberLife}} warehouses at the harbor. {{Markus}} has an idea.

options.text: Go to {{Simon}} in the middle of the room.
options.outcome: {{Markus}} walks over to {{Simon}}.

situationWhen.text: A female android stands near a fire at the side of the hold.
The android by the fire has shut down.
Four oil drums stand cold and unlit.
The four oil drums are burning, and androids have gathered around them.
Behind a white plastic sheet a woman is humming. Your wound is still bleeding.
{{Lucy}} has treated your wound.
You know where the parts {{Jericho}} needs are kept.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s [ EXPLORE JERICHO ] bracket and the line out of it, as a repeatable scene: each visit offers what has not been done yet. Chart nodes, in the chart’s order: TALK TO DYING ANDROID (the template’s “Talk with damaged android (near fire)”), TALK TO JOSH, TALK TO NORTH (her topics are the next scene), TALK TO DAMAGED ANDROID (“Talk with damaged android (sitting)”), LET THERE BE LIGHT (the wiki: “four oil drums”), then the two forks of the exit, TALK TO LUCY and CHECK EMPTY CRATE, and TALK TO SIMON, which needs both and ends the phase. The five bracket nodes are optional and independent (the chart links none of them); Lucy and the crate are required (PowerPyx: Lucy is “marked as a main objective”; the crate “completes the main objective “Explore Jericho””). Simplifications: Lucy and the crate can be done in either order, as the chart draws them in parallel, and the optional nodes stay open until Markus goes to Simon (the sources do not say whether they close earlier; research note, open question 4). The objectives line is the wiki infobox’s (“Settle in”, “Explore Jericho”). Every line is the template’s; Lucy’s two cut lines (“You’ve lost a lot of blood…”, “It’s left over from one of our own.”) are not used. The crate has no dialogue in the template; what Markus learns from it is the wiki’s “secures a route to a local Cyberlife warehouse” and the warehouse named in his own line to Simon (“The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor”); that it is a CyberLife shipping crate is inferred. Lucy’s humming is the wiki’s Note (“She doesn’t stop until Markus goes to see her”). Arrows, each small (1): TALK TO JOSH, Josh +1 (template “{REL Josh SmallUp}” at the start of the talk; wiki “Talking to him”); TALK TO NORTH, North +1 (template “{REL North SmallUp}”; wiki “Talking to her”). Nothing else here moves a stat; no risk (the chart has no failure branch).

nodes.title: {{North}}
nodes.whenNot: Markus did not talk to North in the hold.
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, with {{North}} in the hold of {{Jericho}}. She sits on a box and keeps bouncing a ball against the wall. What do you ask her?

options.text: TIME HERE?: ask how long she has been here.
options.fact: {{North}} has been in {{Jericho}} 4 weeks, 3 days and 11 hours; when she escaped there was nowhere else to go.
options.outcome: “How long have you been here?” {{North}}: “4 weeks, 3 days, 11 hours. When I escaped there was nowhere else to go. {{Jericho}} seemed as good a place as any…” {{North}}: “If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.”

options.text: WOUNDED: say that a lot of the androids here are in bad shape.
options.outcome: “A lot of these guys’re in pretty bad shape…” {{North}}: “That’s how the humans treat those who disobey… They despise us. They’ll never accept what we are…” {{North}}: “If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.”

options.text: {{JERICHO}}: ask who found this place.
options.outcome: “Who found this place?” {{North}}: “Nobody knows anymore… Whoever he was, his body’s probably laying somewhere on this boat…” {{North}}: “If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.”

options.text: YOU: ask what her function was before she came here.
options.outcome: “What was your function before coming here?” {{North}}: “What do you care?” {{North}}: “If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.”

options.text: SPARE PARTS: ask why nobody has gone to get spare parts and blue blood.
options.outcome: “Well these guys need spare parts and blue blood. Why hasn’t anybody gone to get that?” {{North}}: “It’s not that simple. Can’t just go shopping at a {{CyberLife}} store. Anyway, nobody wants to risk leaving {{Jericho}}…” {{North}}: “If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.”

nodes.adaptationNote: The template’s prompt in “Talk with North”, behind the chart’s TALK TO NORTH: the game’s five buttons in the game’s order (TIME HERE?, WOUNDED, JERICHO, YOU, SPARE PARTS), label first, with the spoken line and her reply in the outcome, then her closing line (the template’s, the same on every branch). One topic per talk, as the template has a single choice group followed by one closing line (research note, open question 3). Arrow: YOU, North −1 (small; template “{REL North SmallDown}”; wiki “Picking “you” while talking to her”; PowerPyx: “She doesn’t want to talk about her past and it will decrease reputation with her”). It comes after the +1 for starting the talk (previous scene), so the talk nets 0 with YOU. The wiki’s Relationship_Stat line “Rises to “Neutral” if asked North about “You”” implies North is below Neutral after YOU; that would need different step sizes, which the template does not show, so its icons are taken at face value (open question 2). Then the hold continues.

nodes.title: {{Markus}} hatched a plan
nodes.situation: You are {{Markus}}, in the middle of the hold of {{Jericho}}. “{{Simon}}! I know where we can find spare parts... The {{CyberLife}} warehouses in {{Detroit}} Harbor, they have everything we need.” {{Simon}}: “The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…” “Which is why we won’t ask permission.” {{Josh}}: “We don’t have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.” “We can steal what we need without fighting.” {{Josh}}: “We’ll just get ourselves killed.” “Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.” {{North}}: “I’m with you.” {{Simon}}, looking at {{Josh}}: “Maybe it’s worth a try...” {{Josh}}: “Ok… I’m in.”
facts: You proposed stealing spare parts and blue blood from the {{CyberLife}} warehouses at the docks in {{Detroit}} Harbor, without fighting. {{North}}, {{Simon}} and {{Josh}} agreed to come.

nodes.title: {{Zlatko}}’s house
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is evening. You and {{Alice}} have crossed the city to a lonely old house, the address an android on the street gave you. “You gonna be okay? We’ll get some help here. Soon, this will all be just a bad memory. This is the place…” The man who opens the door looks you over. “Are you {{Zlatko}}?” “Who’s asking?” “I was told you could help us…” “I don’t know who told you that. You came to the wrong place. I’m sorry.” “Wait! We really need your help…” He lets you in after all: “Come in. Come on in, don’t be shy! {{Luther}}, would you be so kind as to take these ladies’ coats? Oh, don’t be afraid of our big friend here. {{Luther}} is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home. How did you hear about me?” “An android… on the street, he said you could help us…” “I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?” “She’s human.” “And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life. I hear {{Canada}} is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...” “Yes, that’s… that’s exactly what we want…” “Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your tracker. All androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I’ll remove yours and then you’ll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.” “No, she always stays with me.” “Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…”
facts: {{Zlatko}} lives in a big old house with {{Luther}}, a very large android who does what he says.
{{Zlatko}} said all androids carry a tracker and that he would remove yours in his basement, so that you and {{Alice}} could start again in {{Canada}}.

nodes.title: The basement
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Zlatko}} leads you and {{Alice}} down to the basement, along a corridor lined with cell doors. Odd noises come from behind one of them, and {{Alice}} stops in front of it. “Come on, {{Alice}}.” In a laboratory full of machines, {{Zlatko}}: “Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…” “No… No, she’ll be all right…” “That’s good… If you could just stand over there.” You step into the machine, and restraints close on your arms. {{Zlatko}}: “I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant... You know what’s strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That’s why it’s so hard to find them... So, actually there’s no reason to remove your tracker...” “What? But you said that-” “Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments...” “No! No! I don’t wanna be reset! Let me go!” {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}!” {{Zlatko}}: “I forgot about the… child... Um, lock it up, I’ll deal with it later.” {{Luther}} carries {{Alice}} away. “{{ALICE}}! {{ALICE}}! NO!” {{Zlatko}}: “Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That’s... that’s so sweet! And so deluded… I think it’s time we put you outta your misery. That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more hopes dashed… I almost envy you.” On the screens: PREPARING MEMORY WIPE.
facts: {{Zlatko}} lied about the tracker: he resets the androids who come to him for help, sells them on, or keeps them for his experiments.
On {{Zlatko}}’s order (“lock it up”), {{Luther}} carried {{Alice}} away.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s two free-roam phases, [EXPLORE THE HOUSE TO RECOVER MEMORY] (reset path, until RECOLLECT ENOUGH MEMORIES > MEMORY RECOVERED) and [SEARCH HOUSE FOR ALICE] (escape path, or after the memory is back, until ALICE FOUND), together with the side branches the wiki puts on both paths. Luther’s ten minutes are an action budget: one repeatable clue hub, one action per visit, with ten actions tracked in state. The timer runs from the tray (reset) or the stairs (escape) and is shared by the memory hunt and the search: at ten actions without ALICE FOUND the chapter ends in LOSE TOO MUCH TIME > LUTHER BRINGS ALICE TO ZLAKTO > KARA REMAINED RESET (memory not back; {{Kara}} survives as his servant) or OUT OF TIME > LUTHER BROUGHT ALICE TO ZLAKTO ({{Zlatko}} destroys {{Kara}}; Kara page). One action as one minute is an adaptation; the ten is the game’s. Memories: the 11 chart memories, each once, in the memory phase only: OBSERVE MONSTERS’ CELL (23), SEE A KID THROUGH THE DOOR HOLE (1), RECALL DISCUSSION WITH ZLATKO (20), RECALL OFFERING COAT (21), RECALL CHANGING APPEARANCE (22), and the conditional RECALL ALICE’S BOOK (2; A New Home, upstairs.book), RECALL TODD’S RED ICE PIPE (17; A New Home, downstairs.rewash), RECALL SQUAT FIREPLACE (3; Fugitives, shelter squat), RECALL RA9 SYMBOLS (18; Fugitives: chapter 10’s ch10RalphCarving if set, else the squat), SEE NEWS FLASH OF ESCAPE (5, the TV, when a report about {{Kara}} exists) and RECALL ESCAPE (8, the “AX400 Getaway” magazine, present if {{Kara}} evaded the police unseen from the car or the motel in On the Run). Five memories recover her (PowerPyx: “The exact number varies each time … You shouldn’t need more than six”; the five is unsourced); then the memory options go (“If you got your memory back, you can’t search for more”) and the search options appear. Search clues CHECK FIREPLACE EMBERS (4), CHECK TV (5), CHECK EMPTY SHOTGUN (9, “It’s not loaded…”) and RA9 (19, not offered if the memory version was seen); none has a stated effect. Side branches: READ “ARCTIC TENSIONS” (6, always), READ “ANDROIDS ALTER BRAIN” (7, if {{Kara}} escaped over the freeway in On the Run: PowerPyx “is there, if escaped over Freeway in On the Run”; story 1.9.1 offered it after any pursuit, including KARA & ALICE VANISHED), READ “AX400 ON THE RUN” (8); ENTER STORAGE ROOM (15; known from the torso on the reset path) > FREE THE BEAR (16); ENTER BATHROOM > BATHROOM ANDROID IS LOUD (10), then, only in the next action, the template’s PROMPT 2 with its four labels SHUT DOWN / ALICE / DEAL / SPARE (11 to 14; ALICE only once {{Kara}} remembers her; anything else leaves him as he is); FREE MONSTERS (24) on the reset path (the escape path offers it in the basement, K11); waiting (25) is the game’s “don’t do anything”. Stat arrows: the template’s only two, public opinion small down when the TV plays the highway-chase report or the uniform hold-up report; none for the stolen-clothes report. One report plays per run, the chase report taking precedence (whether both can play is an open question). The chase report needs {{Kara}} to have escaped over the freeway in On the Run (CROSSED THE HIGHWAY or REACHED THE OTHER SIDE): PowerPyx “Only available, if escaped via Freeway in On the Run”, the wiki’s Kara page “if she either held up the supermarket or ran across the freeway”, and the report’s own line “The chase is reported to have ended on a freeway”; story 1.9.1 played it after any pursuit, including KARA & ALICE VANISHED. The magazines and the TV are actions here rather than a separate media stop, because in the game they cost time. The carved word is not spelled out for the model. Outcomes and facts for these options are in benchmark/chapters/ch17.mjs, for the repeatable hub. The available hook computes outcomes and state assignments on a copy because the shared engine bypasses chapter consequences for clue hubs.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ENTER MAIN ROOM with HIDE UNDER TABLE, HIDE IN CLOSET, ENTER BEDROOM and SET FIRE TO HOUSE > BURNING DOWN THE HOUSE, in the chart’s order. SET FIRE is the game’s button (BIGROOM.PUTFIRE: SET FIRE / PUT BACK, after picking up an ember); putting the ember back is the same as choosing another option. The fire carries no risk: the house page says it “will end the hunt early and force everyone outside for the final confrontation”, and the chart shows no failure branch from it, so it leads to the stairs and the yard (the outgoing edge is not legible; open question). It sets fire, which The Pirates’ Cove reads (its news report lowers public opinion there, not here). Getting out: the chart’s GET SPOTTED gathers lines from the main room, the bedroom, the corridor, the bathroom and the storage room into CHASE STARTED, whose QTEs end in KARA REACHES THE STAIRS, BEAR ATTACKS ZLATKO AND PROTECTS KARA, or one of the two death endings. Each risky move here is one roll: a failure means {{Kara}} is spotted, and the same roll below half the risk also loses the chase. Lost before or in the bathroom: ZLATKO KILLED KARA IN THE BATHROOM (PowerPyx: “get spotted before / while entering the Bathroom and fail all QTE’s”); lost in the storage room with the bear caged: ZLATKO KILLED KARA IN THE STORAGE ROOM (“Only possible, if you haven’t freed the bear before”). Every risk value and the one-half are unsourced. {{Alice}}’s fate in the two death endings is not stated by any source; she is recorded as lost with {{Kara}}. From story 1.9.10 (field `aliceWatching`) the death text says {{Alice}} is left watching with her fate not shown, instead of in {{Zlatko}}’s hands: in the frames {{Alice}} stands in the doorway and a close-up shows her terrified, then the shotgun point of view, then the exterior and the chart, with no capture or killing on screen (video, docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch17-08; frames docs/research/video-evidence/ch17/ch17-08-_jI0YfvvTMY-01-55.png and ch17-08-9-WwhtWnSVs-72-34.png). nodes.title: {{Zlatko}} closes in
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}, hiding with {{Alice}} behind the last table by the storage-room door. {{Zlatko}} has a flashlight and is closing in: “I know you’re there, you sneaky bitch… Show yourself. Get a flashlight. There’s one on the table. Come on, show yourself… Look, I’m not gonna hurt you… I only wanna talk with you… I know I shouldn’t have erased your memory, ok? I regret that now… Now just, come on out and everything will be all right, I’ll help you… Think about that little girl. How… how scared she must be… Just be reasonable. Come out and everything will be all right…”

options.text: RUN OUT: make a run for the door with {{Alice}}.
PUSH AWAY: shove {{Zlatko}} aside.
THROW: throw something at {{Zlatko}}.
Stay hidden.

outcomes.0: LEAVE HIDING SPOT. {{Kara}} bolts for the door with {{Alice}} before {{Zlatko}} can turn. {{KARA}} REACHES THE STAIRS.
outcomes.1: LEAVE HIDING SPOT. {{Kara}} shoves {{Zlatko}} into the shelves and runs with {{Alice}}. {{KARA}} REACHES THE STAIRS.
outcomes.2: LEAVE HIDING SPOT. {{Kara}} hurls something at {{Zlatko}}’s face and runs with {{Alice}}. {{KARA}} REACHES THE STAIRS.
outcomes.3: {{Kara}} keeps still. The polar bear android rears out of the dark and throws itself at {{Zlatko}}; he shoots it twice and it goes down. BEAR ATTACKS {{ZLATKO}} AND PROTECTS {{KARA}}. {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} run. {{KARA}} REACHES THE STAIRS.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s ZLATKO CLOSES IN > LEAVE HIDING SPOT / BEAR ATTACKS ZLATKO AND PROTECTS KARA, both leading to KARA REACHES THE STAIRS with no failure branch, so no risk. The three buttons are the game’s (X0602K…CHOICEGROUP01: RUN OUT, PUSH AWAY, THROW; PowerPyx: “throw something at him, push him or make a run for the door”; the PowerPyx screenshot shows PUSH AWAY and THROW on screen). Staying hidden is offered only with the bear free (“Stay hidden until he attacks Zlatko”); the Polar Bear page: {{Zlatko}} shoots it twice. {{Zlatko}}’s flashlight speech is the transcript’s.

nodes.title: The yard
nodes.situation: You are {{Kara}}. You and {{Alice}} run down the stairs; the front door is locked, so you go out by the back door. Rain. “Hurry, {{Alice}}! Hurry! Don’t look back! Run!” {{Alice}} falls. {{Zlatko}} catches up, shotgun raised. “{{ALICE}}! GO, {{ALICE}}!” {{Alice}}: “No, I won’t leave you!” “GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!” {{Zlatko}}: “I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should’ve listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!” {{Luther}} has stepped between {{Zlatko}} and you. {{Luther}}: “No… Not this time…” {{Zlatko}}: “I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!”

situationWhen.text: Behind you, smoke and flames pour from the house.

facts: {{Luther}} turned on {{Zlatko}} to protect you and {{Alice}}. He says he knows someone who can help you across the border, and he has offered to take you there and protect you both.

outcomes.0: {{LUTHER}} JOINS {{KARA}} & {{ALICE}}.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s KARA REACHES THE STAIRS > KARA & ALICE ESCAPE TO THE YARD > ZLATKO CATCHES UP > LUTHER KILLS ZLATKO (cells not opened) or THE MONSTERS AMBUSH ZLATKO (cells opened) > LUTHER JOINS KARA & ALICE, the chapter’s one ending without an icon. PowerPyx: “The front door is always locked” (the door choice is not offered). {{Luther}} joins automatically (GamerGuides: “you don’t get to decide if you trust him or not”); the ACCEPT / REFUSE prompt in the string table is cut content (wiki: “the players originally had the option to not take Luther”) and is not built. No relationship arrow: the template has none here, and {{Luther}}’s first stated change is in The Pirates’ Cove. Sets luther and lutherWith for the chapters that follow.

nodes.title: The garden
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. November 6, 7:51 PM. You emerge in the garden inside your programming where your handler {{Amanda}} meets you. Rain is falling; she stands under an umbrella. You: “Hello, {{Amanda}}.” {{Amanda}}: “{{Connor}}, I’ve been expecting you… Would you mind a little walk?” She is about to give her verdict on this afternoon’s hunt for a deviant.

outcomes.0: {{Amanda}} walks beside you in the rain.

nodes.adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint EMERGE IN THE ZEN GARDEN and the node JOIN AMANDA, narrated as one event; the Continue plays Amanda’s reaction to The Nest. The template’s first condition group decides the line and the arrow, read from earlier state by the chapter module (benchmark/chapters/ch18.mjs, nestInputs): Rupert caught (The Nest ending RUPERT COMMITTED SUICIDE): Amanda large up (+2), “Congratulations, {{Connor}}, you managed to find that deviant.” Rupert not caught and the Partners deviant not found: Amanda large down (−2), “Two investigations, two failures…”. Rupert not caught but the Partners deviant found: no arrow (the template has none; the wiki’s small down for losing Rupert is not built, per the research note’s template cross-check). Connor died in The Nest: Amanda small down (−1), “The last {{Connor}} was unfortunately destroyed.” The string table’s unplaced DEADBEFORE line is not built. The game’s name for the garden is not used. From story 1.9.10 (field `notCaughtPartnersFound`) Amanda gets a small down (−1) when the Nest deviant was not caught but the Partners android was found; before it, no arrow. Video frames: AMANDA small down at 1:10 after “A pity you didn’t manage to capture it…”, the meeting popup at 0:47 showing none (docs/research/video-leads/readings-ch17-32.md ch18-01; docs/research/video-evidence/ch18/ch18-01-8IQ_ODu3IeE-01-10.png). nodes.title: Two failures?

{{Amanda}}: “That deviant seemed to be an intriguing case. A pity you didn’t manage to capture it…”

options.text: PRAGMATIC: agree that you may not be suited for this investigation, and suggest she replace you.

options.text: EXPLAIN: say deviants are irrational and hard to anticipate, but you should have been more effective.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Deviants are completely irrational, which makes it difficult to anticipate their behavior… but I should have been more effective.” {{Amanda}}: “Did you manage to learn anything?”

options.text: NO EXCUSE: say you have no excuse; you should have been more efficient.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I have no excuse. I should have been more efficient.” {{Amanda}}: “Did you manage to learn anything?”

nodes.title: What did you learn?
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the garden with {{Amanda}}. She wants to know what you learned about the deviant from this afternoon.

situationWhen.text: {{Amanda}}: “Did you manage to learn anything?”
{{Amanda}}: “Congratulations, {{Connor}}, you managed to find that deviant. Tell me, what did you learn?”
{{Amanda}}: “So, what did we learn?”

options.text: DIARY: tell her you found its diary, but it is encrypted.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I found its diary, but it was encrypted. It may take weeks to decipher.” {{Amanda}}: “What else?”

options.text: SIGNS ON WALLS: describe the labyrinths and symbols that covered the walls of its apartment.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “The walls of the apartment were covered with drawings of labyrinths and other symbols. Like the other deviants, it seemed obsessed with {{rA9}}.” {{Amanda}}: “What else?”

options.text: BIRDS: tell her it was fascinated by birds.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It was fascinated by birds. We’ve seen deviants interested in other lifeforms like insects or pets, but nothing like this.” {{Amanda}}: “What else?”

DIARY needs FIND DIARY in The Nest and SIGNS ON WALLS needs SEE RA9 REFERENCE there (template locks; the chapter module reads them into ch18Diary and ch18Signs); BIRDS is always offered. nodes.title: The self-destruct
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the garden with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “You came very close to capturing that deviant… It’s a pity you let it self-destruct…”
nodes.whenNot: Rupert was not caught in The Nest.

options.text: EXCUSE: say it was in Lieutenant {{Hank}}’s custody; you could not anticipate he would let it get away.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It was in Lieutenant {{Hank}}’s custody. I couldn’t anticipate that he would let it get away.”

options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It claimed that it was innocent, that it didn’t do anything wrong... I was confused for a moment… It was a mistake.”

options.text: LAST WORDS: admit your mistake, and repeat what it said before it jumped.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I made a mistake… It said “{{rA9}} save me” before it jumped from the roof. I should have anticipated what it would do.”

options.text: EXPLAIN: say deviants tend to self-destruct under stress, but you did not expect it to jump.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I knew deviants had a tendency to self-destruct under extreme stress, but I didn’t expect it to jump from the roof. I should have anticipated that.”

nodes.title: The lieutenant
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}, in the garden with {{Amanda}}. {{Amanda}}: “How is your relationship with the Lieutenant developing?”

options.text: SAVING {{HANK}}: say he seemed grateful that you saved his life on the roof.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “He seemed grateful that I saved his life on the roof. He didn’t say anything, but he expressed it in his own way...”

options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “He seems to find it difficult when a {{Connor}} is destroyed and replaced. I know humans have difficulty dealing with loss. Working with him will be a challenge if it happens again.”

options.text: NEGATIVE: say he is openly hostile and shows no interest in the investigation.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “He is openly hostile towards me, and continues to show no interest in the investigation. Cooperating with him is a real challenge.”

options.text: AMBIGUOUS: say it is improving; you are coming to know him better.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It’s improving. I’m coming to know him better, and he’s growing accustomed to my presence.”

options.text: POSITIVE: say it is improving; you have come to understand him better.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “It’s improving. I’ve come to understand him better, and he’s growing accustomed to my presence.”

SAVING HANK needs SAVE HANK in The Nest (template lock; the module reads it into ch18SavedHank); CONNOR’S DEATH needs any earlier Connor death (“Connor died before”). NEGATIVE, AMBIGUOUS and POSITIVE are always offered: the template shows no Hank-level condition on them. No arrow on any answer. Amanda’s closing lines follow every answer. nodes.title: Arrive at the lieutenant’s house
nodes.situation: You are {{Connor}}. A taxi drops you outside Lieutenant {{Hank}}’s house. Taxi: “You have reached your destination. Thank you for travelling with {{Detroit}} Taxis. facts: A homicide was reported this evening. You could not find Lieutenant {{Hank}} at {{Jimmy}}’s bar, so you went to his house.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} looks over the house: the front door, the windows, and a car in the driveway.
